newsitem.title: UK: Charts point way for dollar/mark to extend gains.
newsitem.headline: Charts point way for dollar/mark to extend gains.

text.p: The dollar's relentless climb higher against the mark shows little sign of abating and chartists see near-term gains extending to 1.64 marks and even up to 1.70 in the weeks to come.

This bullish view has been reinforced by the dollar's clearance of several key chart points over the last week which has also made the risk of a big correction increasingly remote, technical analysts said.

"Dollar/mark has now passed three important technical milestones: the October 1992 pullback line at 1.59 marks, the downtrend line drawn from the June 1989 high of 2.0475 at 1.5935 marks and the psychologically important level of 1.60," said Andrew Chaveriat, technical analyst at Paribas in London.

Furthermore, on Friday the dollar cleared major resistance in the 1.6060 marks area, a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of its February 1994 peak of 1.7686 to the record low of 1.3430 marks in March 1995.

On Monday, the U.S. unit cracked another significant chart level, breaking convincingly above the top of a rising channel around 1.6150 marks that was seen capping dollar gains since October 1995. At 1253 GMT it was at 1.6265 marks.

While the risk of a dollar retreat has not entirely disappeared, analysts said the recent clearance of such major hurdles is likely to keep any corrective action relatively light with these previous resistance levels now acting as supports.

"Big support should be building up near 1.6080 marks, look to hold on this on sustained dips," said Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank in London. "Further out, we're still aiming for 1.68 marks and higher but clearing the 1.6330/6400 zone will be key."
The 1.63 mark point is an important psychological level but analysts said a previous support area in the 1.6320-30 zone from May 1994 will provide a sterner upside test.
Analysts also cautioned that markets may have to show a little patience for further gains with the dollar likely to take a breather around the 1.63 level before pushing higher.

"With the break above 1.60 marks the market is getting comfortable with these levels above here," said Andy Hart, technical analyst at Standard Chartered Bank in London. "We're likely to see it oscillating within the 1.60-1.63 zone before zooming higher."
Although he expects some near-term corrective action, Standard's Hart still sees dollar/mark as a buy on dips with an upside objective of 1.67 marks.

Momentum indicators, such as the 14-day relative strength index (RSI), are showing overbought conditions and may serve to dampen the dollar's ardour, but some technicians expressed doubt that this would be significant factor in pressuring the dollar.
"Although momentum indicators are in overbought territory, no divergence exists, suggesting further gains are likely," said Alan Dunne, technical analyst at Bank of America in London.
Analysts also point out that these types of indicators are more suited to picking turning points in ranging markets and are less reliable when markets are in well-defined trends.

Nevertheless, a slight dollar retracement at current levels is seen as being necessary to provide a stronger base to extend its gains. Above the 1.63-1.64 zone, there are few significant chart points to impede its progress up to 1.70 marks, analysts said.
